A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MDNS research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–F. Corresponding material can be reliably matched; v2 additionally includes a NeurIPS checklist.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices D–F report original Ising and Potts sampling experiments, comparisons, ablations and UDNS results.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experimental results in Section 4 and Appendices D–F, including sampling metrics, training curves and ablations.

M1.justification: The MDNS construction, RERF/LV/CE/WDCE objectives, replay-buffer procedure and sampling algorithms are unchanged. The UDNS extension already appears in v1; the new fine-tuning suggestion does not introduce an implemented procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same 4 × 4 and 16 × 16 Ising distributions and 16 × 16 three-state Potts distributions across the same temperatures. Newly discussed fine-tuning and cited combinatorial-optimization applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: LEAPS and Metropolis-Hastings remain the principal comparators, Swendsen-Wang supplies reference samples, and Appendix D.5 retains the DRAKES experiments. Added citations do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training budgets, architectures, sampling procedures and evaluation metrics remain unchanged in Section 4 and Appendices D–F. These include the 50k-step Ising and 100k-step Potts training schedules and their existing warm-up phases.

E4.justification: The loss comparisons, warm-up ablation, resampling-replicate sensitivity study, preconditioning analyses, DRAKES failure study and UDNS analyses are retained unchanged. V2 adds no new robustness or supplementary experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests. V2's checklist explicitly acknowledges the absence of error bars, but does not change the statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–6 and Figures 1–18 retain their results and findings. For example, low-temperature MDNS ESS remains 0.981 for Ising in Table 1 and 0.933 for Potts in Table 3. Relocated displays do not represent new results.

T1.justification: Appendix C.1 corrects Q_t(y,d) to Q_t(y,x) in the Kolmogorov forward-equation derivation. This is a local formula correction; the theoretical guarantees and proof arguments otherwise remain unchanged. The noise-rate condition explicitly added to Section 2.2 was already stated in v1's Lemma 2.

C1.justification: The central claims about the SOC-based MDNS framework, differentiability-free objectives, scalable WDCE training and high-dimensional sampling performance are retained. The added fine-tuning suggestion is explicitly future work, not a new demonstrated contribution.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly suggests extending the framework to fine-tune pretrained discrete diffusion models using potentially nondifferentiable rewards. Section 4.1 also defers a systematic warm-up study to future work. Existing result interpretations and applicability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository location in the abstract, reiterated in the checklist; v1 lacks this access information. Existing architecture, hyperparameter, hardware and runtime disclosures are unchanged. Repository contents and availability cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations covering combinatorial-optimization diffusion methods, Proximal Diffusion Neural Sampler, DriftLite, TR2-D2 and distribution-matching policy optimization. These modestly update context and future-work links without substantially changing the positioning relative to PIS or LEAPS.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized language corrections, fixes the reversed sequence-length/vocabulary-size description, formats contributions as a numbered list, updates publication and funding text, and appends a checklist. The main narrative and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 moves from page 8 to page 9, and Figure 2 moves from page 9 to page 10, alongside other text reflow. Scientific display contents and structures remain essentially unchanged; no experimental figures or tables are added or removed.

improvement.justification: V2 provides a previously absent code location, corrects local notation and prose errors, and makes the contribution list easier to scan. These improve documentation and readability, while the experiments, results and substantive theoretical guarantees remain stable. The gains are limited rather than a substantial strengthening of the research.
